headline: Jalen Johnson scores 26 points with four steals as Hawks overcome slow start to beat Hornets 111-97
text: ATLANTA -- — Jalen Johnson scored 26 points, Aaron Wiggins bailed out Atlanta's depleted backcourt with 19 points and the Hawks overcame a slow start to beat the Charlotte Hornets 111-97 on Friday night in an NBA Cup game. The Hawks took their third straight win and have won eight of their last 11 games. The Hornets have lost four straight and 10 of 11. Moussa Diabaté led the Hornets with 21 points and 14 rebounds. Brandon Miller had 19 points. Johnson and Dyson Daniels , who leads the NBA in steals and deflections, each had four steals. The Hawks had 12 steals and took a 36-16 advantage in points off turnovers. Daniels had 11 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds. Charlotte took a big lead of 14 points at 50-36 in the second quarter in a much different game than the Hawks' 128-81 rout of the Hornets on Oct. 23 in the biggest blowout in Atlanta franchise history. The Hornets led only 57-56 at halftime and the Hawks leaned on their defense and 3-point shooting to pull ahead in the third quarter. Johnson's 3 gave Atlanta a 68-65 lead and a steal by Daniels set up a jam by Johnson for a 76-69 lead. The Hawks outscored the Hornets 31-19 in the third to take an 87-76 lead into the final period. The Hawks' backcourt was limited as rookie Kingston Flemings (back) missed his third straight game and CJ McCollum (calf) was out for the second straight game. McCollum is expected to miss four weeks. Center Jock Landale (back) also was held out. Wiggins moved into the starting lineup with 14 points in Atlanta's 117-112 win at Oklahoma City on Wednesday night. Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 17 points. Up next Hornets: Host Memphis on Monday night. Hawks: Host Detroit on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Franz Wagner scores 35, hits late jumper to lift Magic over Nets 113-111
text: NEW YORK -- — Franz Wagner scored 35 points, including a game-winning jumper with 2.4 seconds left, and the Orlando Magic beat the Brooklyn Nets 113-111 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night. Facing his older brother and former teammate Mo Wagner for the first time after spending their last five seasons together in Orlando, Franz Wagner stepped back and hit a 14-foot jumper steps away from the Nets bench. Brooklyn called a timeout and Julius Randle had a chance to win it but missed a 28-foot 3-pointer. Franz Wagner shot 13 for 25 from the field and made 7 of 9 free throw attempts, including a pair in the opening minute of the second quarter when he was fouled by Mo Wagner, who signed with the Nets as a free agent in July after eight seasons in Orlando. Desmond Bane finished with 21 points, reserve Nikola Vucevic chipped in 15 points and Anthony Black had 13 for the Magic, who have won five of their last six games. Randle scored 27 and Danny Wolf , who started in place of Egor Demin , added 20 points for the Nets, who have lost their last four games. Brooklyn fell to 1-6 at home this season after going 12-29 last campaign at Barclays Center. Orlando appeared to have the game under control after Jalen Suggs hit a 3-pointer for a 106-104 lead with 3:22 remaining. On the next possession, the Nets used one of their challenges that overturned an offensive foul on Mikel Brown Jr . He was credited with a basket and was awarded a free throw that evened the game at 106. Randle later hit a jumper and Bane answered with a 3 that made it 109-109. Randle then converted a pair of free throws before Wendell Carter Jr . tied the game with a putback layup with 31 seconds left following Franz Wagner’s errant 3-pointer before he made up for it before time expired. Up next Magic: At Washington on Sunday. Nets: At Minnesota on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: James Harden posts 26th 50-point game, moves past Kobe as Cavaliers beat Pacers 128-119
text: CLEVELAND -- — James Harden scored 51 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night. It was the 18-year veteran guard's 26th 50-point game, passing the late Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games in NBA history. It was Harden's first since he had 55 points for the Los Angeles Clippers against the Charlotte Hornets on Nov. 22, 2025. Harden is the sixth player to have a 50-point game for Cleveland. It was also his best scoring game with the Cavaliers since being acquired near the trade deadline in February, surpassing the 36 he had against Chicago last season. Harden was 15 of 26 from the field, including 7 of 11 from beyond the arc. He also made all 14 of his free throws along with six rebounds and six assists for the Cavaliers, who have won three of four and improved to 2-1 in East Group B. Donovan Mitchell added 20 points. Peyton Watson , who missed Wednesday's game due to a lower back contusion after being injured on Monday against Chicago, scored 15. Ivica Zubac had 21 points and 10 rebounds and Pascal Siakam scored 21 for the Pacers, who have dropped three straight and fell to 1-2 in East Group B. Cleveland was up 74-73 four minutes into the third quarter before going on a 21-4 run over a nearly four-minute span. Harden scored 13 during the spurt as he made all four of his shots from the field, including a pair of 3-pointers. The Cavaliers' largest lead was 113-90 with 7:39 remaining before the Pacers countered with a 21-4 run to make it a two-possession game with 2:03 left. Mitchell ended the spurt though with a basket on the ensuing trip. Up next Pacers: At New York on Sunday. Cavaliers: At Chicago on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Davis and Dybantsa help the Wizards knock off the Bulls 98-94 in NBA Cup action
text: CHICAGO -- — Anthony Davis had 36 points and 11 rebounds, and the Washington Wizards beat the Chicago Bulls 98-94 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night. AJ Dybantsa had 20 points, 10 rebounds and six assists for Washington, which posted its second straight win after an eight-game losing streak. Trae Young scored 16 points, and Kyshawn George finished with 11. The Wizards grabbed control with a 12-0 run in the fourth quarter, highlighted by a reverse jam by Dybantsa in transition. The No. 1 pick in this year's draft capped the spurt with a layup that made it 89-78 with 7:31 left. Chicago closed to 96-94 on Nic Claxton 's two free throws with 43 seconds left. Norman Powell had a chance to tie the game in the final seconds, but he missed a floater and Young made two foul shots at the other end. Powell scored 16 points for Chicago, and Buddy Hield had 15. The Bulls, who lost 124-120 to Washington in their home opener on Oct. 24, led by as many as 15 in the first half. The Bulls dropped to 1-2 in NBA Cup action. The Wizards are 2-1 with one game left in group play. Washington opened the third quarter with a 15-2 run, taking a 67-62 lead on Davis' layup with 5:56 left. Young made a go-ahead 3-pointer during the stretch. The Wizards carried a 75-69 lead into the final period after outscoring the Bulls 23-9 in the third. The Wizards also controlled the third in the first meeting of the season, outscoring the Bulls 40-20 in the quarter. Chicago played without rookie Caleb Wilson , who missed his fifth straight game. The 6-foot-10 forward had surgery on his right hand on Nov. 12. Up next Wizards: Host the Orlando Magic on Sunday night. Bulls: Host the Denver Nuggets on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scores 40 as Thunder beat Pelicans 126-120 in NBA Cup
text: OKLAHOMA CITY -- — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points and the Oklahoma City Thunder rallied in the fourth quarter for a 126-120 win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday night to improve to 2-1 in NBA Cup play. Gilgeous-Alexander's 3-point play with 34.8 seconds left gave Oklahoma City, which trailed by 16 points in the third quarter, a 124-116 lead. Rookie Aday Mara added 22 points on 11-of-15 shooting and had 16 rebounds for the Thunder. Jared McCain and rookie Bennett Stirtz each scored 18 points for the Thunder, who are 8-5 since the loss of three starters to long-term injuries. Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears scored 22 points each for New Orleans, which fell to 0-3 in NBA Cup play. New Orleans fell behind 11-0 then outscored the Thunder 64-45 to lead 64-56 at halftime. Williamson led the Pelicans with 18 points but picked up his third foul with less than a minute to play when he sent Gilgeous-Alexander to the floor. The two-time league MVP was slow to get up, which quieted the home crowd. He made both free throws to finish the half with 19 points. A 3-pointer by Herb Jones, his fourth of the game, gave New Orleans a 91-76 lead with four minutes left in the third quarter. But Oklahoma City responded with a 16-7 run fueled by back-to-back baskets by Stirtz and a 3 by Gilgeous-Alexander to pull to within 98-92 to start the fourth. The Thunder pulled even at 102 on a 24-foot shot by McCain with 9:22 remaining and took a 108-102 lead on a basket by Isaiah Hartenstein . Up next Pelicans: Play at San Antonio on Saturday night. Thunder: Play at Miami on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Devin Booker scores 23 points and Suns pull away in final minute for 111-101 win over Jazz
text: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Devin Booker had 23 points and the Phoenix Suns scored the final six of the game to pull away late and beat the Utah Jazz 111-101 in an NBA Cup matchup Friday night. With the Suns clinging to a four-point lead in the final minute, Booker made a basket and a free throw and Jalen Green added a dunk and another free throw to clinch Phoenix's fifth victory in six games. Miles Bridges and Dillon Brooks each had 18 points, and Collin Gillespie scored 16 for the Suns (8-7). After back-to-back wins in Los Angeles over the Clippers and Lakers, the Jazz reverted to the form they displayed in their earlier 12-game losing streak — poor shooting, sloppiness with the ball and weak defense. Darryn Peterson had 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists to pace Utah (3-14). Jaxson Hayes added 18 points and 14 boards, while Brice Sensabaugh also scored 18. The Suns led by double digits most of the game before the Jazz pulled to 96-89 on a twisting layup by Hayes with 6:25 left. Green responded with five straight points, but the Jazz made one last run — a 9-0 surge — that made it 105-101 with 39.5 seconds remaining on Svi Mykhailiuk 's 3-pointer. The Jazz are still missing their starting frontline of Lauri Markkanen (hand), Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson Jr . (knee). Without any interior presence to contend with, the Suns applied a full-court press at times and their defensive ball pressure disrupted Utah's offensive sets on the perimeter. Utah committed 14 turnovers, leading to 19 Phoenix points. The Suns have won 13 of the last 14 matchups. Brooks made a 3 to cap a 15-4 run that gave Phoenix a 39-27 lead with 9:30 left in the second quarter. Up next Suns: Continue their six-game trip Monday at New Orleans. Jazz: Host the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Nikola Jokic's big 2nd half sends the Nuggets to a 133-124 win over the Rockets
text: DENVER -- — Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets defeated the Houston Rockets 133-124 in a back-and-forth NBA Cup game Friday night. Christian Braun and Cameron Johnson each scored 19 for the Nuggets in a matchup that featured 32 lead changes and 17 ties. Neither team led by more than five until there was 2:01 remaining. The win was Denver's sixth in eight games, the past two of which have come against the Rockets and Boston Celtics , who are a combined 23-9. Aaron Gordon added 18 points for the Nuggets, while DeMar DeRozan scored 15 and Jamal Murray had 14 points and seven assists. Jokic scored 24 points in the second half, including 18 in the third quarter. Alperen Sengun , who played the first quarter in goggles after sustaining a scratched cornea in a win Wednesday against Indiana, led the way for Houston with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for his second triple-double this season. Each of the Rockets’ starters finished with at least 16 points, including 25 from Fred VanVleet , who also had nine assists. Their backups, however, provided only 12 points and combined to miss 13 of 17 shots. After a 20-foot jumper by VanVleet extended Houston’s lead to five with 5:10 left, Denver countered with 10 straight points in 1:55 and finished the game on a 23-9 run. The Nuggets improved to 2-0 in the group stage of the NBA Cup, while the Rockets dropped to 1-2. It was the second meeting in 11 days between the teams. Houston won the first one, 110-100, on Nov. 9. Up next Rockets: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday. Nuggets: At the Chicago Bulls on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Luka Doncic scores 25, Lakers barely hold off Kings 106-104 on LaVine's miss at the buzzer
text: LOS ANGELES -- — Luka Doncic had 25 points and eight assists, Quentin Grimes hit a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 57 seconds to play, and the Los Angeles Lakers rallied in the fourth quarter for their 10th win in 11 games, 106-104 over the Sacramento Kings on Friday night. Walker Kessler scored 15 points and Matisse Thybulle had 14 for the Lakers, who struggled at home against another rebuilding opponent two nights after their nine-game winning streak ended with a loss to the Utah Jazz . The Lakers hung on for their fifth straight home victory over Sacramento when Zach LaVine missed a long 3-pointer at the buzzer. De’Andre Hunter scored a season-high 30 points and hit five 3-pointers for the Kings, who dropped to 1-14 on the season — the worst 15-game start in team history — with their eighth straight loss despite taking a lead into the fourth quarter. Sacramento led by 11 in the third quarter and took a small advantage into the fourth, but the Lakers built a 101-93 lead with 4 1/2 minutes to play. The Kings responded with eight straight points to tie it on Domantas Sabonis ' free throws with 2:32 left. After Grimes made his only 3-pointer of the night, Doncic made a turnover with 23 seconds left. Kessler then bricked two free throws to give the Kings one last chance, but LaVine pulled up and clanged his final shot off the rim. LaVine scored 19 points. Sabonis had 19 points and 16 rebounds for Sacramento, and Darius Acuff Jr . had 18 points and 12 assists. The Lakers improved to 2-1 in NBA Cup play. Sacramento is 0-3. Austin Reaves missed his fourth straight game with a bruised heel. The Lakers’ second-leading scorer has already missed five of their first 17 games due to injury after missing 31 games last season. Kessler’s first 3-pointer in a Lakers uniform put LA ahead early in the fourth. Precious Achiuwa sat out for Sacramento with a leg injury. Up next Kings: Host Boston on Saturday. Lakers: Host Utah on Monday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
